title: mark_resumed_never_stamps_a_submitted_draft_test cannot fail — strip already NULLs the token, so the by-token mark matches nothing with or without the submitted_at guard
detail: The N26 'never on a submitted draft' boundary is advertised as pinned, but strip_draft_on_submit NULLs continue_token (asserted in strip_on_submit_empties_payload_keeps_metric_test: draft_field(db, vacancy_id, "continue_token") |> should.equal("")). mark_draft_resumed_by_token("tok-sub") matches zero rows regardless of any submitted_at guard, so the test passes even if that guard were deleted. The claimed invariant is not exercised.
recommended_fix: Seed via raw SQL a row with submitted_at set but continue_token intact, then assert mark_draft_resumed_by_token leaves resumed_at NULL — or drop the guard claim from the section banner.

title: W8 erased-draft exclusion is proven by the NULLed token, not by erased_at — the erased_at filter arm of list_resumable_draft_tokens is never isolated
detail: One UPDATE sets erased_at AND continue_token = NULL together, so the row is excluded by the token-IS-NOT-NULL condition alone. If the SQL's erased_at IS NULL filter were removed, this test still passes — that arm of the 'live only' contract has no independent failing path.
recommended_fix: Set erased_at while keeping continue_token in a second raw UPDATE (or separate draft), asserting it is also excluded, so each filter arm has its own failing path.

title: resume_on_closed_vacancy_renders_closed_page_test asserts only absence of resume markers — a blank or broken 200 page passes
evidence:
resp.status |> should.equal(200)
  let body = simulate.read_body(resp)
  body
  |> string.contains("data-apply-page=\"form-resume\"")
  |> should.be_false
  body |> string.contains("draft-resume-banner") |> should.be_false
detail: The test name claims the closed page is rendered, but there is no positive assertion of any closed-page content (closed copy or its data-apply-page marker). Any 200 body lacking the two resume strings — including an empty or wrong page — satisfies the test.
recommended_fix: Add a positive assertion for the closed vacancy page's marker or copy (e.g. its data-apply-page value) alongside the two negative assertions.

title: W7 fixture contradicts its own comment: 'never rented skips eviction' but never_rented_before is false and has_eviction_history is supplied
detail: The comment says the fixture relies on the never-rented path to skip eviction, yet the fixture sets never_rented_before to false and provides has_eviction_history anyway. The comment misdescribes the data the test actually submits.
recommended_fix: Either correct the comment to describe the fixture as-is, or set never_rented_before to "true" and drop the eviction field so the fixture matches the claim.

title: seed_draft_with_token's UPDATE has no email predicate — it rewrites continue_token on every draft row for the vacancy, and its 'tok-seed' candidate is always overwritten
evidence:
let assert Ok(_) =
    pog.query(
      "UPDATE application_draft SET continue_token = $1
       WHERE vacancy_id = $2::uuid",
    )
    |> pog.parameter(pog.text(token))
    |> pog.parameter(pog.text(vacancy_id))
    |> pog.execute(db)
detail: The helper upserts one draft then rewrites continue_token for ALL drafts on the vacancy (no email clause). On a multi-draft vacancy (as built later in the W8 test) a second call would silently clobber other drafts' tokens. The 'tok-seed' upsert candidate is dead weight — always replaced by this UPDATE.
recommended_fix: Add AND email = 'tenant@example.com' to the UPDATE, or pass the desired token straight to upsert_application_draft and delete the redundant UPDATE.

title: form_view_now_ms and near_future_date are single-use 1:1 wrappers; the form_view import exists only to be renamed
detail: Each wrapper delegates unchanged to the underlying function and is called exactly once (loaded_at and desired_move_in_date). The form_view import is used nowhere else. Pure indirection with no abstraction value — same class as round-1 N4.
recommended_fix: Call form_view.current_unix_ms() and test_helpers.near_future_iso_date() directly at the two call sites and delete both wrappers.

title: W6 section banner is missing the closing separator line every other section in the file has
detail: Every other section header in this file (Helpers, Save, W5, W7, W8, W9, N21, N26, etc.) is bracketed by // ==== lines above and below. The W6 header has only the top line, so the test function visually merges into the banner.
recommended_fix: Add the closing // ============================================================================ line under the W6 title to match the file's banner convention.
